title: Failure Modes: Why Agents Break
service: FailTag: failure-mode detectors for agent traces, a directory store with one JSON file per trace and an atomically replaced last-known-good baseline, a CI gate and baseline drift alerts with per-mode cooldowns, an online tagger that reports findings as RFC 5424 syslog lines, and cascade radius over the trace's data-dependency DAG
runtime: Python 3.10+, standard library, pytest; no agent, no LLM, no network: every trace is data written in the test, a step uses an earlier step's result by writing ${N} in its arguments, and the clock is a function the test injects
deviations_from_plan: Part 1: the timing defect sits in detect_cascading_errors (references() recomputed for every failed step x later step) instead of detect_context_loss, because a per-step precompute there would still be O(constraints x steps) and could not give 8x on both sides; the constraint defect is parse_constraint returning Rule(tools=None) for an unknown verb, which surfaces as a TypeError in violates

Part 1: the scope-creep example is 'summarize the credit memo' (edit inside credit) rather than 'find the update notes', since update is a whole word there and word matching would not change the verdict
Part 2: the baseline pointer is a BASELINE file holding the ordered list of last-known-good trace ids; traces are named by the sha256 of the tid so '/' and case-only differences are safe
Part 3: alerts are rate-limited per mode; the lesson's traces carry no cluster id, so the mode is the cluster

Part 4: the main traps are the per-trace checks of 'gates at every step' (state kept per tid while traces interleave, each mode once per trace, success_hallucination only at End with SUCCESS_VERBS, PRI = FACILITY * 8 + SEVERITY); the tag_online docstring spells out the SD-PARAM escape order, since escaping the escape character first is already a main Part 4 trap elsewhere in this chapter
Part 5: besides radius and root causes, the report has depth (longest dependency chain) and the systems reached, taken from dotted tool names such as billing.charge

parts.lesson_anchor: The five industry-recurring modes; code/main.py detect_scope_creep (substring w in request), detect_context_loss (the word after 'do not' used as a token) and detect_cascading_errors (every call after an error counted as downstream)
planted_bugs: mentions matches write verbs with re.search(verb, request), a substring match: 'summarize the credit memo' contains 'edit', so an unrequested write is not scope creep

parse_constraint returns Rule(tools=None) for a verb missing from VERB_TOOLS ('do not exceed 5 searches') instead of None; the TypeError surfaces in violates, two calls from the root cause (tag -> detect_context_loss -> violates)
detect_cascading_errors counts every later call with any reference as downstream, although the docstring counts only calls that reference the failed step
once that is fixed, every failed step recomputes references() for every later step, O(S^2)
parts.timing_assert: tag() on a 4000-step trace under 0.12 s. Measured on this machine with other jobs running (load average 4 to 15): the quadratic version 1.17-2.22 s over 29 runs and 1.25-2.54 s inside the checker runs (at least 9.8x the limit), 4.2 s in a checker run at load average 22; the fixed version a median of 3.0-3.3 ms over 4000 runs (36x under the limit), the slowest of each 400 runs 6.7-26 ms. A half fix that caches references() but keeps the double loop is still O(S^2) at 42-127 ms, so it passes or fails with the load; INTERVIEWER.md tells the interviewer to ask for the one-pass count
parts.overfix_guard: write verbs must match whatever their case or punctuation ('Edit the README.', 'then SAVE.'), which rules out split() and a match without lower(), and only as whole words ('list the saved searches' is scope creep), which rules out a leading-only \b and startswith; parse_constraint itself must return None for an unknown verb, which rules out patching violates around Rule(tools=None); a consumer 1999 steps after the failure must still count, which rules out a look-ahead window; a call that uses the failed result twice is one consumer, which rules out counting ${N} occurrences; only tool calls count, per failed step ('look up both invoices'), which rules out counting a message or one counter pooled over every failure

parts.lesson_anchor: Where failure monitoring goes wrong: No baseline (drift detection needs a last-known-good); Ship It (detectors wired to a trace store)
parts.exactness: stored as one JSON file per trace under traces/ plus a BASELINE file replaced atomically (temporary file in the same directory, then os.replace); a trace comes back equal as dataclasses: nested args with lists, dicts, None, 0.1 + 0.2 and a 20-digit integer, status, a result with a line break, a tab and non-ASCII text, the step kinds, and labels in their original order; the baseline comes back in order after a reopen, including the tid 'run/7\n' that ends in a newline
traps: the tid used as the file name ('run/7\n' becomes a subdirectory: FileNotFoundError)
percent-encoded file names colliding for 'T001' and 't001' on a case-insensitive file system (macOS, Windows; Linux does not catch it)
steps read back as dicts
labels sorted or turned into a set
tids() in file-name order instead of sorted by tid
baseline() raising FileNotFoundError before a baseline is set
a baseline with unknown tids accepted
the baseline written in place, so a failing os.replace does not fail the update
the temporary file left behind when the replace fails
the baseline written before its ids are checked (a rejected baseline must not be stored)
BASELINE stored one id per line (the tid 'run/7\n' loses its newline)

parts.lesson_anchor: Where failure monitoring goes wrong: No baseline, Over-alerting (cluster and rate-limit); Exercise 5 (fail the build if >=5% of traces tag a mode)
traps: clean traces left out of the denominator
the gate using > instead of >=
the gate comparing count >= threshold * n (0.07 * 200 = 14.000000000000002)
no baseline treated as all zeros instead of LookupError
a rolling baseline that swallows a slow 4% -> 8% -> 12% climb
abs() making a falling rate page
one cooldown shared by every mode
a suppressed alert restarting the cooldown
the cooldown boundary (exactly cooldown_s later must page)
min_traces off by one
a repeated label counted twice in mode_rates
a rate exactly tolerance above the baseline paging (>= instead of >)
the cooldown counted from the first page only (setdefault)
alerts in first-seen order instead of sorted by mode
parts.integration: the lesson's seven traces (t004's later calls changed to use the failed search's result) are tagged by Part 1, stored by Part 2 and confirmed as the baseline; seven later traces that write and break 'do not modify any files' page context_loss and scope_creep from 2/7 to 1.0, and every mode in the lesson set fails the 5% gate

parts.lesson_anchor: Mitigation: gates at every step (per-step checks); main.py's 'detect early, stop the loop'; Use It (findings go to an observability platform)
parts.wire_format: RFC 5424 syslog, one record per line ending in a newline, decided by the test's regex '<PRI>1 TIMESTAMP HOST APP PROCID MSGID [failtag@32473 name="value" ...] MSG' and a strict unescape that only allows \", \\ and \]; PRI = 16 * 8 + severity; TIMESTAMP in UTC with milliseconds and Z; the tag_online docstring gives the escape order (backslash first, then the quote and ]), so the tid b"]\ and the tool magic"scan] are an incidental check
traps: reported modes or failure state shared between interleaved traces: one reported set swallows c's scope_creep
one reported set reset at every Start (a's write after c starts reports scope_creep and context_loss again), or failed steps shared across traces (a's ${1} is its own step)
one step counter for all traces (odd's ${1} no longer names its own failed search)
a mode reported again on later steps of the same trace (a's second write raises scope_creep and context_loss again next to tool_misuse)
modes deduplicated within one step only, or only one finding per step (a's first write reports scope_creep and context_loss, in DETECTORS order)
success_hallucination only decidable at End, carrying only the tid (no step, no tool)
success_hallucination checked with WRITE_VERBS ('make a README')
End used only to drop the trace, so success_hallucination is never checked
PRI as facility + severity, as severity * 8 + facility, or the two numbers written side by side (163)
the step index counted from 1
a timestamp without milliseconds
a timestamp in local time (caught only when the machine is not on UTC)
tool_misuse left out of the online checks (a's second write has no content)
messages counted as consumers, or one consumer counter pooled over every failure (the quiet trace stays silent)
lines held back until the feed ends (the probe counts pulled events)
a plain coroutine instead of an async generator

incidental: param values escaped in the order the docstring gives (backslash first, then the quote and ]); only the double quote escaped, the quote escaped before the backslash, ] left unescaped or json.dumps breaks the record for the tid b"]\ and the tool magic"scan]
clarifying_questions: order of findings from one step

parts.lesson_anchor: Exercise 3 (cascade radius: given a failure at step N, how many downstream steps did it affect); 'a phantom SKU hallucination triggers four API calls, a multi-system incident'; 'Cascading is the killer'
traps: every failure reported as a root, or roots found by looking only at direct parents (the email.send failure is two hops from the root)
a diamond counted twice
messages left out of the radius, or counted as systems
depth as the shortest hop count instead of the longest chain
a step reached by two roots counted for only one
self, forward and missing references accepted
recursive DFS hitting RecursionError on a 3000-step chain
a root cause nothing used left out (radius 0, depth 0)
the traversal stopping at a downstream failure (relay: email.send is reached only through the failed payments.refund)
references not checked when the trace has no failure
